name: ai-seo
cost: Free (MIT). The paid monitoring tools it mentions are optional
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf and any agent that supports the Agent Skills spec
short: Helps your agent make your content easier for AI search engines to find, quote and cite in their answers.
what: This skill turns your agent into an AI search adviser. It starts with an audit: check your key queries in Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity, see who gets cited, and test your pages for clear answer blocks, sources, schema and crawler access. Then it works through structure, authority and presence on third-party sites, with notes on files like `llms.txt`.
who: Marketers, founders and writers who want their site to show up in AI answers. It's part of a 50-skill marketing pack, so you can install just this one. If you only need a classic technical SEO audit, the pack's `seo-audit` skill is the better fit.
needs: Node.js, to run `npx skills`, or Claude Code or Codex for the plugin route

steps.title: Install just this skill
steps.text: The CLI asks which agents to install into. To get the whole pack, leave off `--skill ai-seo`.

steps.title: If you run it from inside Claude Code
steps.text: Run from inside an agent session, the CLI may only install to `.agents/skills/`, which Claude Code doesn't read. Name the agent instead.

steps.title: Or install the pack as a Claude Code plugin
steps.text: Then run `/plugin install marketing-skills`. This installs all the marketing skills.

steps.title: Add your product context (optional)
steps.text: The skill first reads `.agents/product-marketing.md` if it exists. The pack's `product-marketing` skill creates it, so the agent asks fewer questions.

try.label: A first prompt
try.text: "How do I show up in AI answers? Audit our site's AI visibility for our top queries."

watch: The stats in the skill change fast. The skill itself says to re-check them before quoting them to a client.
It points to paid tools such as Semrush, Ahrefs, Otterly and Peec AI for tracking. The skill also gives a manual monthly check if you don't want any.
The README lists paid partners who fund the library. It says they don't change what the core skills recommend.
